q: A crew member goes over the side on a broad reach. What is the very first thing you shout and do?
answer: "Man overboard!" — throw the danbuoy and horseshoe, point at the casualty
why: Flotation first and a spotter who never looks away.

figure.note: Casualty astern to port

ru.Casualty astern to port: Человек в воде слева за кормой

q: Both yachts are sailing. Who gives way?
answer: You — you are on port tack, she is on starboard
why: Rule 12: port tack keeps clear of starboard tack.

q: Both yachts are on starboard tack. Who gives way?
answer: You — you are the windward boat
why: Rule 12: same tack, windward keeps clear of leeward.

q: You are motor-sailing with the engine in gear. A yacht under sail alone is crossing from your starboard. Who gives way?
answer: You — under power you are a power-driven vessel
why: Rule 3: sail plus engine = power-driven; show the cone by day.

figure.note: Your engine is running and in gear

q: Motoring, you see a motorboat crossing on this bearing, which has not changed for five minutes. What do you do?
answer: Give way — alter course to starboard, early and clearly, and pass astern of her
why: Rule 15: she is on your starboard side, so you keep clear; avoid crossing ahead.

figure.note: Bearing steady at 050° relative

q: Two motor yachts are meeting head-on in a channel. What do you do?
answer: Alter course to starboard; pass port side to port side
why: Rule 14: both turn to starboard.

q: Under sail you are catching up a slow motorboat from astern. Who gives way?
answer: You — the overtaking vessel always keeps clear
why: Rule 13 overrides sail-over-power.

figure.note: You are faster, approaching from well abaft her beam

ru.You are faster, approaching from well ab: Вы быстрее и подходите далеко позади её траверза

q: Wind F5 blowing against a 2-knot current in the strait you are about to enter. What sea do you expect?
answer: Short, steep breaking seas — worse than the wind suggests
why: Wind against tide shortens and steepens the waves.

figure.note: Wind from the north · current setting north at 2 kn

ru.Wind from the north · current setting no: Ветер с севера · течение на север 2 уз

q: Reversing out of the berth the stern swings to port by itself. What is happening and how do you use it?
answer: Prop walk from a right-handed propeller — berth port-side-to and use a burst astern to pull the stern in
why: A right-handed prop kicks the stern to port in astern.

figure.note: Engine astern, rudder centred: stern walks to port

ru.Engine astern, rudder centred: stern wal: Задний ход, руль прямо: корму забрасывает влево

q: You are coming back to the man overboard under power. How do you make the final approach?
answer: Slowly, heading into the wind; neutral as they come alongside near the bow
why: Into the wind you stop easily; a turning prop next to a swimmer is lethal.

figure.note: Final approach under power, wind from ahead

ru.Final approach under power, wind from ah: Последний заход под мотором, ветер с носа

q: You need to know which tack you are on. On this heading, what is it?
answer: Port tack
why: The tack is named after the side the wind comes over; tacks apply on every point of sail.

q: You are on a dead run with the main boom out to starboard. Which tack are you on?
answer: Port tack
why: On a run the tack is the side opposite the main boom.

figure.note: Dead run, main boom to starboard

q: The skipper asks where the other yacht is. How do you call it?
answer: Abeam to starboard
why: Abeam is 90° from the bow; starboard is the right-hand side facing forward.

q: A ferry is coming up from this direction to overtake you. How do you call its position to the crew?
answer: On the starboard quarter
why: The quarter is about 45° abaft the beam, between the beam and the stern.

q: Your lookout spots a fishing boat here. How should she call it out?
answer: On the port bow
why: The bow is about 45° either side of dead ahead; port is the left side.

q: A small motorboat is close to your heading line, a little to the right. How do you report it?
answer: Fine on the starboard bow
why: "Fine" means close to the bow line; "broad" means nearer the beam.

q: A RIB is following in your wake. Where is it?
answer: Dead astern
why: Directly behind the stern is dead astern.

q: You and another yacht are sailing side by side. Which boat is the windward boat?
answer: The other yacht
why: The windward boat is the one nearer the wind, upwind of the other.

q: A crew member feels seasick and wants to be sick over the side. Which side do you send them to?
answer: Port, the leeward side
why: Always to leeward, downwind, so it blows away from the boat.

q: A gust heels the boat hard. The skipper calls "everyone to windward!". Where does the crew sit?
answer: Port side, the high side
why: Windward is the side the wind comes from; crew weight there reduces heel.

q: Your crew want to swim off the stern. What do you rig first?
answer: A floating line streamed astern
why: A trailing line gives a tired swimmer something to grab before being carried away.

figure.note: At anchor · wind 15 kn · current setting south

ru.At anchor · wind 15 kn · current setting: На якоре · ветер 15 уз · течение на юг

q: The horseshoe is thrown and a spotter is pointing. What do you do at the plotter?
answer: Press the MOB button to mark the spot
why: The MOB button fixes the position at once — vital if you lose sight of the casualty.

figure.note: Crew member just fell in

ru.Crew member just fell in: Член экипажа только что упал за борт

q: How do you keep a proper lookout, sailing like this?
answer: Look under the genoa to leeward regularly
why: Rule 5: the genoa hides the leeward bow — that is where you must look.

figure.note: Deck-sweeping genoa, starboard tack

q: You cannot tell whether the bearing of this motorboat is changing. What do you assume?
answer: That risk of collision exists
why: Rule 7(a): if in doubt, risk of collision is deemed to exist.

figure.note: Bearing hard to read in the swell

q: You must give way to this ship. What kind of alteration does Rule 8 want?
answer: One early turn, big enough to see on radar
why: Rule 8: early, substantial, readily apparent — not a series of small alterations.

figure.note: Bearing steady, range 3 miles

q: You are the give-way vessel but cannot turn to starboard. What do you do?
answer: Slow down or stop and let her pass ahead
why: Rules 8(e) and 16: slowing or stopping is a proper give-way action.

figure.note: Shoal water close on your starboard side

q: You have turned 40° to starboard to pass astern of this boat. What does Rule 8 require now?
answer: Check her bearing until she is past and clear
why: Rule 8(d): check the action until the other vessel is finally past and clear.

figure.note: After your alteration

q: Under sail in this channel, risk of collision with the tanker now exists. Does your duty change?
answer: No — you must still act early not to impede her
why: Rule 8(f): the duty not to impede continues when risk of collision develops.

figure.note: Narrow channel · she can only use the deep water

ru.Narrow channel · she can only use the de: Узкий фарватер · ему доступна только глубокая вода

q: You want to cross this buoyed channel ahead of the ship. What does Rule 9 say?
answer: Do not cross if it will impede her — wait
why: Rule 9(d): do not cross a narrow channel if it impedes a vessel confined to it.

figure.note: Narrow channel · she can only use the channel

ru.Narrow channel · she can only use the ch: Узкий фарватер · оно может идти только по нему

q: In this narrow channel you want to overtake on her port side. What do you sound first?
answer: Two prolonged then two short blasts
why: Rule 34(c): two prolonged + two short = I intend to overtake on your port side.

figure.note: Narrow channel · you are the faster boat

q: In a narrow channel this motor vessel astern sounds two prolonged and two short blasts. What do you do?
answer: Sound agreement and move over to starboard
why: Rule 9(e): if you agree, answer long-short-long-short and make room.

figure.note: Narrow channel · she is closing from astern

ru.Narrow channel · she is closing from ast: Узкий фарватер · оно догоняет вас с кормы

q: Crossing the lane under sail, this ship following the lane is closing on a steady bearing. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — you must not impede a ship in the lane
why: Rule 10(j): sail and vessels under 20 m must not impede power vessels in a lane.

figure.note: Crossing a TSS lane under sail

q: This yacht to windward is running downwind and you cannot see her mainsail. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — you cannot be sure of her tack
why: Rule 12(a)(iii): on port tack, if unsure of a windward boat's tack, keep clear.

figure.note: Her mainsail is hidden behind the genoa

q: Both yachts are close-hauled on port tack and converging. What do you do?
answer: Hold course and speed — she is to windward
why: Rule 12(a)(ii): on the same tack, windward keeps clear; you stand on (Rule 17).

q: You are to windward of this yacht. Who gives way?
answer: She does — she is on port tack
why: Rule 12(a)(i): on different tacks, port keeps clear; windward only counts on the same tack.

q: You are running dead downwind with the mainsail out to port. This yacht is converging. Who keeps clear?
answer: She does — you count as starboard tack
why: Rule 12(b): the windward side is opposite the mainsail, so main to port = starboard tack.

q: You are stand-on to this port-tack yacht a mile away. Your crew want to tack away now, just in case. What do you do?
answer: Hold course and speed so she can keep clear
why: Rule 17(a)(i): the stand-on vessel keeps her course and speed.

q: This motor yacht is coming up from here, faster than you. Who keeps clear?
answer: She does — she is overtaking you
why: Rule 13: from more than 22.5° abaft your beam she is overtaking, whatever the side.

figure.note: She is closing from your starboard quarter

ru.She is closing from your starboard quart: Она подходит с вашей правой раковины

q: You are catching this motorboat up and cannot be sure whether you are overtaking or crossing. What do you do?
answer: Assume you are overtaking and keep clear
why: Rule 13(c): in doubt, assume you are overtaking and keep out of the way.

figure.note: You are faster · about 20° abaft her beam

ru.You are faster · about 20° abaft her bea: Вы быстрее · около 20° позади её траверза

q: You started overtaking this boat from astern; now she is converging with you. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — until you are past and clear
why: Rule 13(d): a later change of bearing does not end the overtaking vessel's duty.

figure.note: Bearing now forward of your beam

q: Sailing downwind, you are catching up this yacht. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — overtaking beats the tack rules
why: Rule 13 overrides Rule 12: an overtaking sailing vessel keeps clear.

figure.note: You are faster

q: Under sail, you see this motor yacht coming up from astern. What do you do?
answer: Hold course and speed — she keeps clear
why: Rules 13 and 17: she is overtaking and keeps clear; you stand on.

figure.note: She is faster, closing from astern

q: Motoring, you meet this yacht under sail end-on. Who takes action?
answer: You alone — power keeps clear of sail
why: Rule 14 is for two power vessels; Rule 18 makes power keep clear of sail.

q: Motoring by day, you see this ship ahead with her masts in line. What do you do?
answer: Alter course to starboard
why: Rule 14: masts in line by day = head-on; both turn to starboard.

figure.note: Her masts are in line

q: Motoring, you see this boat crossing. What do you do?
answer: Hold course and speed, and watch her
why: Rules 15 and 17: you are on her starboard side, so you stand on.

figure.note: Bearing steady, range closing

q: In open water, this high-speed ferry is closing on a steady bearing. Who gives way?
answer: The ferry — you are on her starboard side
why: Rule 15: a high-speed craft is a power-driven vessel with no special priority.

figure.note: Ferry at 30 knots · you are motoring

ru.Ferry at 30 knots · you are motoring: Паром 30 уз · вы идёте под мотором

q: You are the stand-on vessel and she shows no sign of giving way. What do you do first?
answer: Sound at least five short blasts
why: Rule 34(d): five short blasts when in doubt the other is taking enough action.

figure.note: Steady bearing, half a mile, no action

ru.Steady bearing, half a mile, no action: Пеленг не меняется, полмили, никаких действий

q: She still does nothing after your five short blasts. You decide to act. Which way?
answer: Turn to starboard, not to port
why: Rule 17(c): do not turn to port for a power vessel on your own port side.

figure.note: Bearing still steady, closing

ru.Bearing still steady, closing: Пеленг всё так же не меняется, сближение

q: She is now so close that her action alone cannot avoid a collision. What does Rule 17 require?
answer: You must take the best action to avoid her
why: Rule 17(b): when the give-way vessel alone cannot avoid collision, you must act.

figure.note: Very close, still not altering

q: Under sail, you are stand-on to this container ship. Why do you still watch her closely and act early if she does not alter?
answer: She may not see you, and can't turn or stop fast
why: Rules 2 and 17: big ships have blind arcs and long stopping distances.

figure.note: Open water · she is not restricted

ru.Open water · she is not restricted: Открытое море · он ничем не стеснён

q: Motoring, you see this boat crossing on a steady bearing. Who keeps clear?
answer: She does — trolling is not "engaged in fishing"
why: Rule 3(d): trolling lines do not restrict manoeuvring, so Rule 15 applies.

figure.note: Trolling lines astern, no day shape

ru.Trolling lines astern, no day shape: За кормой дорожки, дневного знака нет

q: Under sail near Corfu, this seaplane is taxiing towards your track. Who keeps clear?
answer: The seaplane — it keeps clear of vessels
why: Rule 18(e): a seaplane on the water keeps well clear of all vessels.

q: Motoring, you meet this windsurfer crossing ahead. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — treat her as a sailing vessel
why: Rule 18: power keeps clear of sail; give boards a wide berth.

q: Motoring, you see this trawler crossing from your port side. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — she is engaged in fishing
why: Rule 18(a): power keeps clear of a vessel engaged in fishing, from any side.

figure.note: Two cones, points together

q: In fog, radar shows this target closing. Which alteration is right?
answer: A bold turn to starboard, or slow down
why: Rule 19(d)(i): avoid turning to port for a vessel forward of the beam.

figure.note: Fog · radar only, bearing steady, closing

ru.Fog · radar only, bearing steady, closin: Туман · только радар, пеленг постоянный, сближение

q: In fog, radar shows this target closing from your starboard quarter. What do you do?
answer: Alter to port, away from her
why: Rule 19(d)(ii): avoid turning towards a vessel abeam or abaft the beam.

figure.note: Fog · not in sight, she is faster

ru.Fog · not in sight, she is faster: Туман · судна не видно, оно быстрее

q: In fog, radar shows this vessel closing from your port bow. Are you the stand-on vessel?
answer: No — out of sight, both must act
why: Rule 19: vessels not in sight have no stand-on or give-way; each avoids close quarters.

figure.note: Fog · not in sight of each other

ru.Fog · not in sight of each other: Туман · суда не видят друг друга

q: You were tracking this motor yacht by radar in fog. Now she is in sight. Which rule applies?
answer: The crossing rule — you give way to her
why: Rules 11 and 15: once in sight of each other, the steering rules apply.

figure.note: She has just come into sight, 200 m off

ru.She has just come into sight, 200 m off: Она только что появилась в 200 м

q: Motoring in sight of this ship, you are about to alter to starboard to give way. What signal do you give?
answer: One short blast as you turn
why: Rule 34(a): power vessels in sight signal alterations — one short = to starboard.

figure.note: Clear weather, bearing steady

q: There is no room to turn to starboard for this motorboat. What do you do?
answer: Slow down or stop until she has passed
why: Rules 2(b) and 8(e): when the rule cannot be followed, slow or stop.

figure.note: Narrow passage · rocks close to starboard

q: At night, which of your lights can this ship see?
answer: Only your sternlight
why: The sternlight covers 135° astern; sidelights stop 22.5° abaft the beam.

figure.note: Ship bearing 140° relative

q: You stand with your back to this wind. Where is the centre of low pressure?
answer: To the south-east
why: Buys Ballot, northern hemisphere: back to the wind, the low is on your left.

figure.note: Wind NE · northern hemisphere

q: A thunderstorm cell is approaching against a light easterly. Just before it reaches you, what happens to the wind?
answer: It drops, then a hard gust hits from the storm
why: The cold downdraft spreads out ahead of the storm as a sudden gust front.

figure.note: Cb cell to the west, moving east

ru.Cb cell to the west, moving east: Ячейка Cb на западе, идёт на восток

q: In astern your stern walks to port. You must turn round in a narrow marina fairway. Which way do you turn?
answer: To starboard — astern kicks the stern to port
why: Short bursts ahead with full starboard helm and astern in between both rotate the boat clockwise.

figure.note: Narrow fairway · stern walks to port in astern

ru.Narrow fairway · stern walks to port in: Узкий проход · на заднем ходу корму влево

q: Motoring slowly ahead, you turn to port. Which part of your boat swings towards the moored yacht?
answer: The stern — it swings out opposite the turn
why: Going ahead a yacht pivots about a third from the bow, so the stern swings wide.

figure.note: Turning to port, moored yacht close to starboard

ru.Turning to port, moored yacht close to s: Поворот влево, яхта у причала близко справа

q: Your charter catamaran is stopped in the marina. You want to spin her to starboard on the spot. What do you do?
answer: Port engine ahead, starboard engine astern
why: Twin screws far apart give a turning couple: push one side forward and pull the other back.

figure.note: Catamaran, twin engines · turn to starboard

q: You are on autopilot when a fishing boat appears ahead. You need to steer by hand at once. What do you do?
answer: Press Standby, then take the wheel
why: Standby releases the autopilot drive so the wheel answers you.

q: You see this and hear nothing on the radio. What do you do?
answer: MAYDAY RELAY on 16, then go to help
why: A vessel that cannot call for itself needs you to relay and assist.

figure.note: Red hand flare from this yacht

q: What is the person in the dinghy telling you?
answer: They are in distress and need help
why: Slowly raising and lowering outstretched arms is a distress signal.

figure.note: Person slowly raising and lowering both arms

ru.Person slowly raising and lowering both: Человек медленно поднимает и опускает обе руки

q: What is this yacht asking for?
answer: Assistance — but it is not in distress
why: Flag V: "I require assistance". Distress is NC, flares, MAYDAY.

figure.note: Yacht flying code flag V (white, red X)

ru.Yacht flying code flag V (white, red X): Яхта несёт флаг МСС V (белый, красный X)

q: What does this target on your plotter mean, and what do you do?
answer: Survivors in distress: tell the coastguard and go
why: An AIS-SART marks survivors; report it and assist.

figure.note: Plotter: "SART ACTIVE", 3 miles

q: You want to stay close to the casualty. What do you do at once?
answer: Tack at once, leaving the headsail backed
why: The quick-stop keeps the boat near the casualty.

figure.note: Close reach, crew has just gone over

ru.Close reach, crew has just gone over: Полный бейдевинд, человек только что упал за борт

q: You are sailing back to the casualty. On which point of sail do you make the final approach?
answer: Close reach, easing the sheets to slow down
why: On a close reach you can spill wind to stop and fill the sails to go.

figure.note: Returning to the casualty under sail

q: Where do you make the towline fast on your yacht?
answer: To a bridle between both bow cleats
why: A bridle spreads the load over two strong points.

figure.note: Being towed by the boat ahead
